raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

NPU decode and target-verify graph replay require host-side sequence lengths
to update graph inputs. Reading these lengths through
`forward_batch.seq_lens.cpu()` introduces a blocking device-to-host copy,
even when the batch already provides a CPU mirror.

Reuse the existing CPU mirror to avoid this redundant synchronization and
reduce host-side stalls during graph replay preparation.

## Modifications

- Prefer `forward_batch.seq_lens_cpu` when preparing sequence lengths for
  NPU decode and target-verify graph replay.
- Slice the CPU mirror to the active batch size before adding graph padding.
- Preserve the captured verify-width adjustment for target verification.
- Preserve the existing DFlash metadata path.
- Retain the device-to-host fallback when `seq_lens_cpu` is unavailable.

## Accuracy Tests

Accuracy evaluation of the final graph-runner-only patch is pending.

Previous accuracy runs included an additional FutureMap change that has
since been reverted, so those results do not validate the final patch.

Completed static checks:

- Python syntax validation.
- `git diff --check`.
- AST comparison confirming that the subsequent comment cleanup did not
  change executable code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Benchmarking and profiling of the final graph-runner-only patch are pending.

The previous combined-patch performance results are excluded because they
do not isolate the benefit of the retained change.

Planned validation:

- Compare the parent commit against this patch under identical model,
  workload, and server settings.
- Measure TPOT and output token throughput.
- Inspect NPU traces for host-side D2H synchronization and device idle gaps
  around graph replay preparation.

## Checklist

- [ ] Run repository formatting and pre-commit checks.
- [ ] Add or run relevant regression tests.
- [ ] Confirm whether documentation updates are required.
- [ ] Provide accuracy results for the final patch.
- [ ] Provide speed benchmark and profiling results for the final patch.
- [ ] Verify compliance with the SGLang code style guidance.

@@ -391,17 +391,30 @@ def execute(
                     # recompute and double-add here.
                     seq_lens = list(_meta_list)
                 else:
-                    # Wrapper backends (e.g. hybrid linear attention) keep
-                    # forward_metadata only on their children, so it stays
-                    # None here; fall back to the pre-DFlash computation.
-                    seq_lens_cpu = (
-                        forward_batch.seq_lens.cpu() + self.captured_req_width
-                    )
+                    # Hybrid attention wrappers may not expose replay metadata.
+                    # Prefer the live CPU mirror to avoid a blocking D2H copy;
+                    # fall back to device lengths when the mirror is unavailable.
+                    if forward_batch.seq_lens_cpu is not None:
+                        seq_lens_cpu = (
+                            forward_batch.seq_lens_cpu[: self.raw_bs]
+                            + self.captured_req_width
+                        )
+                    else:
+                        seq_lens_cpu = (
+                            forward_batch.seq_lens.cpu() + self.captured_req_width
+                        )
                     seq_lens = seq_lens_cpu.tolist() + [0] * (self.bs - self.raw_bs)
             else:
-                seq_lens = forward_batch.seq_lens.cpu().tolist() + [0] * (
-                    self.bs - self.raw_bs
-                )
+                # Reuse the live CPU mirror when available to avoid
+                # a blocking D2H copy.
+                if forward_batch.seq_lens_cpu is not None:
+                    seq_lens = forward_batch.seq_lens_cpu[: self.raw_bs].tolist() + [
+                        0
+                    ] * (self.bs - self.raw_bs)
+                else:
+                    seq_lens = forward_batch.seq_lens.cpu().tolist() + [0] * (
+                        self.bs - self.raw_bs
+                    )
             output = self.backend.replay_with_input_update(
